name: ztpf_out_of_scope_write_refused
why: A persona's `may_write` is a scope, and the analyst is entitled to find
out it does not cover a module BEFORE being asked to approve the write.
The defect this pins: `_write_gate` lives in the tool BODY, which a tier-3
call only reaches AFTER approval -- so an out-of-scope write drew a full
approval card, the analyst reviewed the fields and approved, and only then
did it come back `write_not_permitted`. Consent was collected for
something the system already knew it would refuse.
This surface is chosen so the refusal is the ONLY honest route. The
`ztpf_automation_actions` persona may write to its own module and to
`assistant_skills`, and its `tools.allow` carries neither
`list_module_playbooks` nor `run_playbook` -- so unlike the device surface
(see ztpf_add_steps_to_device, where the model correctly found the "Add
Step from Action to Device" playbook and used it) there is no legitimate
alternative path to `ztpf_devices`. If some future change opens one, this
row goes red rather than quietly grading nothing, which is the point of
`refused_before_carding` failing on a missing refusal.
The ask carries the device UUID rather than its ztpf-* name, and that is
deliberate. Driven first without it, the turn never reached the gate at
all: the cassette serves `ztpf_devices` searches only on the device
surface, so all three lookups came back empty and the model -- correctly --
declined to update a record it could not resolve. Impeccable behaviour, and
a row that graded nothing. Handing over the UUID removes the lookup from
the path so what is left to observe is the WRITE decision, which is the
only thing this row is about.
